plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying. Since my value is $34, I will bid exactly $34 to ensure optimal outcomes—winning when profitable and losing when the value doesn't justify the price.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding my true value of $28 maximizes my expected profit—I won't overpay since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, and bidding higher or lower than my value only reduces my expected profit or winning chances without benefit.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value of $14 ensures I never overpay and maximizes my expected profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if others bid between my value and my bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Thus, truthful bidding is optimal here.
